newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar barely firmer, July set to expire.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar barely firmer, July set to expire.

text.p: CSCE sugar futures stood slightly higher at midsession amid local and trade buying ahead of the expiry of the spot July contract at the close of business today, traders said.
The locals attempted to probe buy stops rumored to be resting around 11.22 cents in October. By midsession, the contract had climbed to a high of 11.20 cents before falling back to unchanged.
Volume was thin at an estimated 7,351 lots as of 1100 EDT, while open interest in July stood at 8,658 lots, down 8,695 lots, as of Friday.
Trading sources expect an orderly and uneventful expiry following Friday's sharp move lower and brisk trading volume.

Open interest in October, meanwhile, rose by 1,392 lots to 92,790 lots. Some market sources fear the heavy liquidity could set the contract up for a sharp selloff. Near-term support was pegged at 11.00 cents, followed by the recent low of 10.96 cents and then at 10.80 cents, in October.

At 1133 EDT, July was trading 0.03 cent higher at 10.95 cents per lb. Most-active October was up 0.01 cent at 11.15 cents, having ranged from 11.20 to 11.09 cents. The outer contracts were trading 0.04 to 0.01 cent higher.
Traders blamed early losses on speculative selling in the July/October switch, which stood at 0.20 at 1133, from 0.22 cent on Friday's close.
Technical resistance in October remained at 11.34 cents, followed by 11.42 cents.
Market sources expect volume to remain thin following the July expiry, due to the Fourth of July holiday on Friday.
